# Test-Connectivity

Runs layered network connectivity checks: gateway, internet, DNS and TCP ports.

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| **Changes the system** | No, read-only |
| **Supports `-WhatIf` / `-Confirm`** | Not needed (read-only) |
| **Admin rights** | No |
| **PowerShell** | Windows PowerShell 5.1 and PowerShell 7+ |
| **Source** | [scripts/Test-Connectivity.ps1](https://github.com/lucaswsanchez/helpdesk-kb/blob/main/scripts/Test-Connectivity.ps1) &middot; [tests](https://github.com/lucaswsanchez/helpdesk-kb/blob/main/tests/Test-Connectivity.Tests.ps1) |

## Description

Follows the same bottom-up method as KB-010:

1. Default gateway reachable (ping)
2. Internet reachable by IP (ping, no DNS involved)
3. DNS resolution of the given names
4. TCP connection to the given host:port endpoints (for example Microsoft 365, VPN gateway, file server on 445)

Each check returns an object with Test, Target, Result (Pass / Fail / Skipped), Detail and DurationMs, so results can be filtered, exported or attached to a ticket. A colored summary is printed at the end. The script only reads network state; it changes nothing.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `-DnsName` | String[] | `@('www.microsoft.com', 'login.microsoftonline.com', 'outlook.office365.com')` | Host names to resolve. Defaults to common Microsoft 365 endpoints. |
| `-TcpEndpoint` | String[] | `@('login.microsoftonline.com:443', 'outlook.office365.com:443')` | Endpoints to test as "host:port". Defaults to Microsoft 365 HTTPS endpoints. |
| `-InternetIP` | String | `'1.1.1.1'` | Public IP address pinged to test internet access without DNS. Default 1.1.1.1. |
| `-TimeoutMs` | Int32 | `2000` | Timeout for each ping and TCP connection, in milliseconds. Default 2000. |
| `-SkipGateway` | switch |  | Skip the default gateway check (for example on networks that block ICMP). |
| `-OutputPath` | String |  | Optional path of a CSV file to export the results to. |

## Examples

```powershell
.\Test-Connectivity.ps1
```

Runs all checks with the default Microsoft 365 targets.

```powershell
.\Test-Connectivity.ps1 -DnsName intranet.acme.example -TcpEndpoint 'fileserver01.acme.example:445','vpn.acme.example:443'
```

Tests internal name resolution and access to the file server and VPN gateway.

```powershell
.\Test-Connectivity.ps1 -OutputPath .\connectivity.csv | Where-Object Result -eq 'Fail'
```

Exports all results to CSV and shows only failures.

Real run on the author's home network (private gateway address); public addresses are Microsoft endpoints.

## Notes

Works on Windows PowerShell 5.1 and PowerShell 7+. No admin rights needed. Related KB: KB-009 VPN Does Not Connect, KB-010 Wi-Fi Connected but No Internet.
